body: Fetches a public API's url and answers the shape of its JSON (keys, types, nested objects, a paged answer). With project, component and name it also shows the files generate_resource would write from it.

body: Add an app to a workspace: `nuclear new` makes it in a folder of the workspace and the marker names it. app: its name (its folder); platform: mobile, web or backend; dialect: optional (the platform's default). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

body: Rename an app of a workspace (new_name: its new name). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

body: A new component of the project with its facade (appcomponent).

rows.title: `generate_resource` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests.
body: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests. The fields: from_json (an example answer of the API: a url, which also gives the API, or a file), from_spec (a spec.md: its example answer or its Key | Type table, and its `GET <url>` line), or fields ("id:int name:string origin:Origin?"). source: "rest:<base url>", "rest" or "db" (backend only). actions: of list, get, search, create, update, delete (default: list and get for an API, the rest for a database). dry_run shows the files without writing them. Nothing is overwritten; a name declared elsewhere stops it.

body: A screen of a mobile or web project with its state manager and state model, for a view that is not a list of a resource (generate_resource with screen writes those).

rows.title: `generate_usecase` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing).
body: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing). With calls ("OrderRepository.pending": a method that repository declares) the use case is written too, because it only calls that method. Without calls the use case must already be in the project: one with rules of its own is written first, then this wires it. dry_run shows the files without writing them.

rows.title: `graph_answer` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The exact answer to a question that has one (every command of a tool, the tools of this server and their parameters, the commands that write a kind, a diagnostic by its code, the stages of the Builder, the members of a base type, a version...): the rows of the graph's database, whole, never recalled; then the cards the shelves answer by meaning.
body: The exact answer to a question that has one (every command of a tool, the tools of this server and their parameters, the commands that write a kind, a diagnostic by its code, the stages of the Builder, the members of a base type, a version...): the rows of the graph's database, whole, never recalled; then the cards the shelves answer by meaning. Prefer it to graph_search for "which", "list", "what are the" questions. platform: backend, mobile or web.

rows.title: `graph_search` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind).
body: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind). shelf: concepts (what it is, why, how it works), language (how it is written in Nuclear), platforms (kinds, decorators, layout, plugins), tools (CLI commands, MCP tools, HTTP routes, generators, agents), errors (diagnostics, failures and their fixes), capabilities (what can and cannot be done, limits), playbooks (procedures, roles, skills), examples (validated Nuclear), docs (the long documents: dialects, ADRs, context, status), memory (what agents kept about projects); several separated by commas; "" searches every shelf. platform: backend, mobile, web. kind: a kind's rows (usecase, repository...). type: a row type (diagnostic, kind, cli, playbook...). Each card comes with the rows it links to.

body: Which kind of request this is (a whole system, a component, a resource, one screen, a use case, a rename, a failing test, a question...) and the plan of that kind, step by step with the tool of each step. A paid provider's spending is confirmed by the user twice in the editor (`waiting: spending`), never here. Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask). The factory is for big work: a small or medium task is the agent's own (nuclear_doc("task-size")).

rows.title: The Nuclear MCP server: its tools and how a client must work with them
rows.summary: `nuclear-mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio and gives an AI client 88 tools: the Smart Graph, the compiler, the `nuclear` commands, the generators, the internet and the local developer.
body: NuclearLang (.nuc) and Synapsis, its framework. Nothing about Nuclear is in your training and it is not TypeScript, Dart nor Python: before anything about Nuclear (a .nuc file, the nuclear command, a Synapsis project, a question about them), call nuclear_start. It answers what Nuclear is, the rules never broken, the work cycle on this machine and the atlas of every topic, each read with nuclear_doc. Never search the disk for Nuclear's sources and never guess a syntax. A product is made with these tools: never write target code (TypeScript, Dart, Python) for a feature nor translate code into Nuclear by hand; when a tool cannot do something, say so. Work starts from a workspace (workspace_show of the user's folder; workspace_create and app_add for a new product), and every change of a workspace, an app, a spec or a team is asked to the user first. Then, for a request, call graph_strategy with the user's own words and follow its plan.
